items.title: Research Progress on AI-Driven Biomarker Prediction in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
items.abstract: This study overviews the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in the prediction of biomarkers for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Different from recent reviews on AI-driven radiogenomics that adopt clinical or imaging-based classification, this work innovatively takes AI model architecture as the core classification framework. By analyzing multimodal data (mainly CT) and modeling paradigms (radiomics, deep learning and fusion models), it reveals the current research status centered on EGFR mutation prediction. In terms of technological evolution, prediction models are evolving from traditional radiomics to end-to-end learning, Transformer architecture and multimodal perception-driven deep learning paradigms. This study deeply analyzes the performance differences among different models, fills the application gaps in existing reviews, and provides an important benchmark reference for the clinical optimization of AI-assisted tools and the promotion of standardized precise diagnosis and treatment of NSCLC.

items.title: Rethinking the Development Paradigm in Higher Education: Educational Communication in the Age of Technological Transformation
items.abstract: Abstract. This article critically re-examines the educational “development paradigm” as a foundational methodological assumption of higher education in the context of accelerating technological transformation and artificial intelligence. It is argued that the traditional understanding of development as an inherently positive educational objective requires critical reconsideration. It is demonstrated that human development, technological development, and educational development no longer represent convergent trajectories and therefore should be conceptualised as complementary yet analytically distinct dimensions. Based on theoretical analysis, comparative interpretation, and critical synthesis of interdisciplinary scholarship, the growing divergence between the exponential dynamics of technological innovation and the cognitive, ethical, and communicative capacities of human beings is examined. Particular attention is devoted to educational communication as the principal mechanism through which knowledge is co-constructed, meanings are negotiated, and human agency is sustained within technology-mediated learning environments. The concepts of sustainable development, limits to growth, limits of destruction, posthumanism, and technological singularity are analysed in relation to their implications for higher education. It is substantiated that technological innovation should be evaluated not solely in terms of efficiency and economic performance but also according to its contribution to human flourishing, ethical responsibility, and democratic participation. It is concluded that the educational “development paradigm” should be reconceptualised as a differentiated methodological framework integrating technological progress with human agency, communicative ecosystems, educational communication, and future-oriented education in an AI-mediated society. Keywords: higher education, educational “development paradigm”, pedagogical communication, AI-mediated communication, posthumanism, communicative ecosystems; future-oriented education.

items.title: Retrieval Is the New Record System: A Retrospective Analysis of Open-Source Contributions to Vector Databases and Embedding Infrastructure Underpinning Clinical AI (2025-2026)
items.abstract: Background. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) sits inside many clinical artificial intelligence (AI) prototypes. A language model answers from documents a retrieval layer selects first. If that layer returns the wrong documents, or returns nothing and reports success, the error starts before the model generates a word. Vector databases and embedding tools form that retrieval layer in most designs, so their defects count as health infrastructure defects. Purpose. This study analysed one contributor's public pull request (PR) record in vector database and retrieval projects. It asked three practical questions in sequence. What kinds of defects did the contributions address? What share of the work reached merge? Where did the process break down? Methods. On 21 October 2026 I extracted my full PR record through the GitHub API (author:rtmalikian): 213 PRs across 94 repositories (85 external projects and 9 of the author's own repositories). I defined a subset for vector databases and retrieval infrastructure: 39 PRs across 8 repositories. I coded each PR by status at extraction and read the review threads of seven cases in depth. Two cases from projects next to the subset, cocoindex-io/cocoindex and sentence-transformers, were read for comparison and kept out of the subset counts. Results. Of the 39 subset PRs, 13 merged, 18 were still open, and 8 closed unmerged. Among the 21 resolved PRs, 61.9% merged. Open PRs made up 46% of the subset, the highest share in any part of my record. The merged work clustered around one defect class: silent failure. Code accepted values it should have rejected, dropped errors in background threads, or hid missing data behind a normal response. The hardest case was a long-lived branch. pymilvus #3621 sat open from 20 June 2026 with 12 comments, merge conflicts, and a Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO) gap on a sync commit. Conclusions. The code in this subset was rarely the slow part. Review time was. The fixes that landed shared one pattern: they made a system fail loudly, with an accurate message, at the point where bad data entered. A retrieval system that says "no record found" when it means "the index is corrupt" will mislead a clinician the way a silent defect misleads a developer.

items.title: Robotic Process Automation in Service-Oriented Supply Chains
items.abstract: This chapter examines Robotic Process Automation (RPA) as a digital automation capability for service-oriented supply chains. It explains how software robots automate structured, repetitive, and rule-based tasks across heterogeneous systems, making RPA particularly relevant to service contexts involving order processing, service scheduling, warranty claims, invoice reconciliation, logistics tracking, and customer support. The chapter further clarifies the relationship between RPA and artificial intelligence, arguing that AI acts as an assistive input layer through natural language processing, machine learning, OCR, predictive analytics, and process mining, while RPA remains the primary execution mechanism. Drawing on prior literature and industry examples from logistics, telecommunications, field service, insurance, and product-service systems, the chapter shows that RPA can improve processing speed, accuracy, service consistency, scalability, and employee task reallocation.

items.abstract: The article examines the role of the teacher in developing students’ ability to learn mathematics after the first stage of education within a constructivist framework. Learning to learn is conceptualized as a gradual transition from dependence on the teacher to self-regulation, from supported to independent activity, and from method-oriented instruction to knowledge-centered learning. This process involves cognitive development and the shaping of reflective, conscious participation, in line with the concept of the zone of proximal development, where teacher support is progressively reduced in favour of students’ autonomy. The study was conducted as action research involving 56 fourth-grade students from a public primary school. Iterative instructional interventions enabled examination of the significance of teaching strategies and the organization of the learning environment for students’ cognitive engagement and participation in mathematical activity. The research methods included observation, analysis of students’ work, and unstructured interviews. The teacher is presented as a mediator of meanings, organizer of the learning environment, tutor, and facilitator. The findings highlight the importance of concrete representations, psychological safety, and teacher–student relationships in supporting motivation and students’ learning skills.

items.abstract: Running Persistent AI Worlds (second edition, October 2026) is a review of multi-agent simulations with progressive learning and emergent behaviour: the science of never-ending learning, landmark experiments re-checked, foundation-model-driven open-endedness, societies of language-model agents, learned world models, continual learning and loss of plasticity, the 2026 toolkit, and safety, ethics and validity. Every claim from the February 2026 first edition was re-checked against primary sources, and 248 numbered references link to papers, official lab pages, repositories and package indexes. Two runnable reference simulations in Python and NumPy are included and were run on a 2019 laptop without a GPU: two learning agents in a never-ending seasonal forest (Scenario A), and an evolving population sealed in a fixed energy budget for 1,000 years (Scenario B). Its follow-up, River World on the Desktop (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23338390), joins the two scenarios into one world.

items.title: SAFAR-Onto: A Halal Tourism Ontology Developed Through Hybrid AI–Human Engineering
items.abstract: Halal tourism is a fast-growing market. However, information about halal services, certifications, and facilities is scattered across many sources. Existing tourism ontologies model general tourism concepts such as destinations, activities, and accommodations, but they do not represent Islamic requirements such as prayer facilities, halal certification, or dietary compliance. Manual ontology development is slow. Large language models (LLMs) can speed up concept extraction and hierarchy proposal, but they cannot decide religious or cultural matters. In this article, we present SAFAR-Onto, an OWL 2 DL ontology for halal tourism. We develop it through a hybrid AI–human process across four phases: knowledge acquisition, conceptualization, formalization, and dual validation. The process adapts METHONTOLOGY and Simple Knowledge Engineering. LLMs assist with concept extraction and dimensional analysis. An Islamic studies validation gate routes culturally sensitive decisions to human experts. We evaluate the ontology with two methods: expert review across five quality dimensions, and the OQuaRE technical metrics. SAFAR-Onto contains 10 main classes, 75 subclasses, 201 object properties, and 200 data properties, built from 67 validated domain concepts. Six experts from tourism management, computer science, and Islamic studies rated the ontology between 4.0 and 4.5 on a five-point Likert scale, with accuracy highest at 4.5. Fourteen of 18 OQuaRE metrics scored Excellent or Very Good. We also report a verified mapping from expert feedback to ontology revisions. The ontology is publicly available at https://w3id.org/def/SAFAROnto under a CC-BY-4.0 license. We hypothesize that the development process can transfer to adjacent culturally specific domains such as Islamic finance and kosher food systems.

items.title: Secure Multi-Agent Collaboration Using Large Language Models
items.abstract: As Large Language Models have emerged and become increasingly significant, the way to develop smart multi-agent systems has been transformed, enabling them to communicate, collaborate and decision more efficiently. These systems rely on agents working independently which need to effectively and safely coordinate their actions, to maintain reliability in messy realworld environments. However, bringing LLMs into the mix introduces new risks like data leaks, trickery from bad actors, and trust issues. This paper breaks down a full plan for keeping multi-agent teamwork secure when using LLMs. We look at everything from how they are built and the rules they use to communicate to the safety tools used to stop attacks. We also talk about where this is being used now, the hurdles we still face, and where the tech is headed for building secure AI ecosystems

items.title: Sensor-integrated industrial exoskeletons for ergonomic risk reduction: a systematic review of biomechanical outcomes and intelligent control systems
items.abstract: Introduction Industrial exoskeletons with integrated sensors are emerging as a technology for monitoring biomechanical exposure and supporting the prevention of work-related musculoskeletal disorders in industrial environments. Methods This systematic review followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, retrieving 106 studies published between 2021 and 2026 from the Scopus and Web of Science databases. VOSviewer version 1.6.20 and R‐Studio version 2026.01.2+418 were used for bibliometric and descriptive analyses. The review provides a qualitative synthesis supported by descriptive quantitative reporting of the extracted outcomes. Results The evidence indicated a technological shift from passive devices toward intelligent exoskeletons integrating surface electromyography, inertial measurement units, machine vision, physiological sensors, and artificial intelligence. Individual studies reported maximum reductions of 68.2% in muscle activity, 34% in spinal compression, and up to 60% in muscle fatigue, alongside productivity improvements of up to 59.5%. Machine learning approaches achieved an ROC of 0.985, automated assessment accuracies of 98.5%, and posture estimation with an ICC of 0.967. However, these values were not pooled estimates and varied across study designs, sensor configurations, tasks, and assessment protocols. Discussion The evidence remains constrained by small sample sizes, sensor drift, interoperability limitations, and insufficient long‐term validation in real‐world industrial environments. Sensor‐integrated exoskeletons show potential for ergonomic monitoring and risk reduction, but their effectiveness and industrial generalizability require further validation through standardized, interoperable, and longitudinal field studies.

items.title: SGXAI_FHO: Spiking Graph Explainable Artificial Intelligence with Fire Hawk Optimizer-based fusion of infrared and visible images under low-light conditions
items.abstract: The traditional methods for fusing images acquired under low-light conditions, in many cases, are unable to retain sufficient integrity of structural and textural features, resulting in a distorted and degraded ability to detect features within a scene. This paper presents a novel approach to overcome these issues by using Spiking Graph Explainable Artificial Intelligence (SGXAI) with Fire Hawk Optimization (FHO) to effectively fuse infrared and visible image data. This new SGXAI_FHO framework uses a combination of Gaussian smoothing algorithms to reduce image noise, brightness, and contrast enhancement techniques on visible images to improve the image quality perceived by the human eye (the observer), as well as cross-modal attention (CMA) mechanisms to extract complementary features from the two input modalities and to prioritize these features during the fusion process. The results of this experimentation provide compelling evidence of the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed framework, achieving an F1-score of 99.81%, precision of 99.46%, recall of 99.72%, and accuracy of 99.56%. These results demonstrate that the SGXAI_FHO framework will provide a robust, reliable, and interpretable approach for low-light image fusion and detection applications and has substantial potential for real-world applications.

items.title: Smart Cold Chains for Perishable Foods: Sensor Fusion, Artificial Intelligence and Dynamic Shelf-Life Management
items.abstract: Food cold chains are increasingly instrumented with connected temperature sensors, intelligent packaging, product-quality measurements and predictive algorithms. Yet the transition from monitoring refrigeration conditions to managing actual product deterioration is neither automatic nor equally reliable across commodities. This critical narrative review evaluates how sensing, multimodal data fusion, artificial intelligence and remaining shelf-life models can support decisions throughout refrigerated food supply chains. Peer-reviewed work published from 2000 to 12 August 2026 was considered, alongside selected foundational studies, through accessible scholarly indexes, bibliographic verification and backward citation examination. Evidence was assessed for biological relevance, measurement validity, independent validation, operational deployment and decision-level consequences. Temperature histories provide an essential but incomplete representation of product condition: packaging atmosphere, initial microbiological or physiological state, humidity, mechanical injury and spatial thermal gradients can materially affect deterioration. Laboratory studies demonstrate promising performance for electronic noses, spectroscopy, flexible indicators and machine-learning models, whereas external route-level validation and calibration across product lots remain comparatively limited. Kinetic models offer interpretable relationships between exposure and quality loss but depend on commodity-specific parameters and assumptions; data-driven models can represent complex patterns but are vulnerable to distribution shift and leakage between training and test samples. Digital-twin and remaining-life allocation studies establish plausible pathways towards first-expired-first-out distribution, yet simulated reductions in waste should not be mistaken for demonstrated commercial benefits. A central distinction is made between marketable quality and microbiological safety: freshness estimates cannot independently establish pathogen absence, extend legally defined use-by dates or replace food-safety controls. The review proposes an uncertainty-aware sequence linking measurement, state estimation, validated remaining-life prediction and constrained operational action. Research priorities include prospective multi-site studies, robust ground truth, calibration transfer, human–algorithm decision trials and transparent accounting of energy, waste and equity. Smart cold chains are best understood as governed decision systems rather than collections of sensors or predictive models.

items.abstract: Global climate change has affected different factors of society, including agriculture, which is one of the key income factors for a country’s economy. Reports predicting the increase in the human population by 2050 have alerted us to the increase in demand in food production required to support this population. This demand can be achieved before 2050 by a hybrid of traditional agricultural practices blended with technology for sustainable agriculture, soil moisture, plant health, pest control, water management, etc. As water scarcity in some regions has risen due to climate change, efficient water management is critical. These systems combine artificial intelligence (AI)-driven automation with precise real-time sensing. This chapter highlights the value and implications of smart irrigation for effective and sustainable farming methods, which is fueled by nanosensors and Internet of Things technologies. Because they track pH and moisture levels and help with nutrient availability, nanosensors are essential to smart irrigation, allowing farmers to apply fertilizer and water more effectively. Such sensors are biodegradable and uses cloud servers and wireless communication to transmit data to the Internet of Things. An automated system that considers the unique requirements of each crop, weather patterns, and soil health is used to process and analyze the data. This system also automatically starts irrigation without human intervention. Proper water management and soil health can promote sustainability and yield crop growth.

items.title: Smart Security and Access Control Systems in Residential Interior Design Projects: A Case Study Approach
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and digital automation technologies have transformed residential environments from conventional living spaces into intelligent ecosystems capable of responding to users’ safety, comfort, and lifestyle requirements. Traditionally, residential security systems were primarily dependent on mechanical locks, physical surveillance, and human monitoring. However, contemporary smart security systems integrate biometric authentication, intelligent surveillance, automated access control, sensor-based monitoring, and cloud-connected platforms to create responsive and adaptive residential environments. This review paper explores the integration of smart security and access control systems within residential interior design projects through a case study approach. The study examines how technological interventions influence spatial planning, material selection, user interaction, and aesthetic considerations in modern residential interiors. A qualitative review methodology is adopted by analysing existing research, technological frameworks, and representative residential applications. The paper evaluates major components including smart locks, biometric systems, video doorbells, motion sensors, AI-enabled cameras, integrated home automation platforms, and cybersecurity mechanisms. The study proposes an integrated design framework demonstrating how security technologies can be embedded within residential interiors without compromising visual quality and spatial experience. The findings indicate that successful implementation requires collaboration between interior designers, architects, technology consultants, and homeowners during early design stages. The paper highlights that future residential interior will increasingly depend on invisible, intelligent, and user-centred security systems where safety becomes an integrated design feature rather than an independent technological addition.

items.title: Sovereign AI in the Developing Global South: Architecting Strategic Autonomy in the Intelligence Economy
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is turning the older digital divide of the developing world into an intelligence-economy participation divide: an asymmetry in the capacity of states to shape, own, govern and draw value from cognitive automation. Read against the literatures on digital colonialism, data extractivism and the "Data Nullius" framework, this article treats Sovereign AI as a distinct policy object for the Global South rather than a subset of digital public infrastructure or industrial policy. It sets out four interlocking registers of sovereignty (compute, supply chain, model and data) and argues for a modular, developmental architecture governed through "fluid institutionalism", built on the principle of foundations before the frontier: connectivity, device affordability and FAIR-aligned digital public infrastructure first, then retrieval-grounded small language models. The article then examines whole-of-government interoperability and tiered human-in-the-loop governance; economic transformation through public procurement; security resilience through inbound and outbound data embassies; local-language models such as Bhashini and InkubaLM; a "choose partners, not sides" posture in a bipolar technology rivalry; and South-South cooperation for a stronger voice in global AI governance. It closes with the binding constraints of energy, water, fiscal capacity and coordination, an assessment of risks including dependency lock-in, elite capture and linguistic exclusion, and a time-phased set of recommendations by institutional actor.

items.title: Sovereign AI in the Developing Global South: Volume III – Conflicts, Insurgencies, and Algorithmic Warcraft vs. Statecraft
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is collapsing the historical separation between statecraft and warcraft. This third volume of the series on Sovereign AI in the developing Global South examines how algorithmic systems are restructuring state authority in domestic governance and armed conflict. It first analyses "algorithmic statecraft": biometric digital public infrastructure and the risk of function creep, with India's Aadhaar and Kenya's Huduma Namba as cases, and predictive policing as a form of actuarial justice that can codify structural discrimination. The article then turns to "algorithmic warcraft": AI decision support systems used for target generation in Gaza, automation bias and the "triage trap" that hollow out meaningful human control, and bias in military AI. It traces the democratisation of lethality through commercial and AI-enabled drones in Myanmar, Sudan, Libya and the Sahel, Bangladesh's border-security modernisation in response to regional spillover, and generative AI as an instrument of cognitive warfare. It closes with the fractured diplomacy of the Global South in the UN Group of Governmental Experts on lethal autonomous weapons systems, and argues that sovereign resilience requires contextualised AI frameworks under strict civilian oversight together with a coordinated push for binding international norms.

items.title: Spatial-Matrix Attention in Atypical Cognition: Full-Grid Dynamic Scanning and Mid-Sweep Directional Switching as a Model for Next-Generation Non-Linear AI Architectures
items.abstract: Standard large language model (LLM) architectures process natural language sequentially using one-dimensional positional encodings and autoregressive causal masks. While effective for localized sequence generation, this serial pipeline creates severe processing bottlenecks during global structural synthesis, cross-modal translation, and parallel error detection. In contrast, neurodivergent human cognitive processing—specifically visual-spatial dyslexic architectures—treats textual and symbolic input as a two-dimensional spatial coordinate plane. Rather than relying on rigid, single-direction visual paths, this cognitive model deploys simultaneous multi-directional raster sweeps: horizontal (left-to-right, right-to-left), vertical (top-to-bottom, bottom-to-top), diagonal X-pattern scans, and dynamic mid-pass directional pivots upon semantic or structural convergence. This monograph formalizes Spatial-Matrix Attention (SMA), an artificial intelligence attention paradigm that replaces one-dimensional token queues with a 2D Euclidean coordinate tensor. By assigning spatial coordinates to tokens and enabling dynamic vector scanning with early-stopping pointer retrieval, SMA allows machine learning models to execute asynchronous parallel drafting, real-time self-proofreading, and low-latency ontological memory access without requiring heavy autoregressive re-evaluation passes. Main Highlights & Key Contributions: 2D Coordinate Embeddings: Replaces standard 1D sequential indexing with a dynamic 2D Euclidean spatial distance matrix and relative angular orientation tensors. Multi-Vector Matrix Rastering: Formalizes vertical column sweeps, cross-planar diagonal scans, and horizontal parsing for global layout and structural density verification. Mid-Sweep Directional Pivoting: Introduces stochastic angle switching and early stopping during raster passes when key semantic thresholds or structural anomalies are detected. Key-Bound Pointer Retrieval: Enables direct execution of pre-cached ontological macros, drastically reducing KV-cache expansion overhead during long-context reasoning.

items.abstract: This multi-volume monograph series introduces Spatial-Matrix Processing, a non-linear language comprehension framework that bridges human visuospatial cognition and next-generation artificial intelligence architecture. Moving beyond the rigid one-dimensional (1D) serial token processing of traditional autoregressive transformers, this work formalizes how language can be evaluated across a two-dimensional (2D) topological canvas. Inspired by the parallel scanning mechanics observed in visuospatial dyslexia—specifically multi-directional raster sweeps (X-pattern, diagonal, and inverse passes)—the framework demonstrates how semantic derivation can bypass sequential token queues in favor of key-bound spatial pointer retrieval. Volume I (Cognitive Architecture & System Blueprint) establishes the human cognitive foundations, contrasting 1D linear attention bottlenecks with 2D spatial-grid parsing. It outlines the architectural design for Spatial-Grid Attention (SGA) and real-time parallel compiling (simultaneous drafting and proofreading). Volume II (Mathematical & Thermodynamic Foundations) provides standalone mathematical rigor, deriving field-theoretic semantic emergence equations, pointer address collision probabilities (P_addr), dynamic resolution throttling algorithms (2D Spatial <-> 1D Linear fallback), and topological conservation under orthographic transposition. It presents the Zero-Entropy Error Transmutation Lemma, proving how structural disorder (such as letter transpositions) can be absorbed and transmuted into high-fidelity semantic intent without information loss.

items.title: Stage aware synthetic generation of high quality human blastocyst images using StyleGAN3 with multi level validation
items.abstract: The lack of large, balanced, and shareable biomedical imaging datasets remains a major barrier to the development, validation, and clinical translation of artificial intelligence systems. Synthetic data generation has emerged as a promising solution, yet its real-world value critically depends on rigorous validation beyond visual realism. In this study, we present and systematically evaluate a stage-aware generative framework based on StyleGAN3 for high-fidelity biomedical image synthesis, using human embryo development in Assisted Reproductive Technology. The StyleGAN3 models are trained to synthesize embryo images at the Start of Blastulation and Blastocyst stages, using a curated cohort of 96 high-quality embryos (selected from an original set of 704 time-lapse IVF videos based on combined ICM/TE Gardner grades of AA, AB, or BA). To assess reliability and practical utility, we introduce a multi-level evaluation protocol integrating distributional similarity (Frechet Inception Distance), frequency-domain spectral analysis, and downstream task-based validation. Experimental results show that the proposed models accurately reproduce global morphological characteristics, with consistently higher fidelity and stability at earlier developmental stages (FID = 52.1), while later-stage synthesis is challenged by intrinsic data imbalance and heterogeneity. Spectral analysis reveals partial smoothing of high-frequency details, highlighting limitations not captured by conventional generative metrics alone. Importantly, downstream experiments comparing real, mixed real-synthetic, and fully synthetic evaluation scenarios using ResNet50 and EfficientNet-B0, with classifiers trained exclusively on real data in all cases, show that synthetic images remain discriminatively informative and occupy a structured, non-degenerate feature space consistent with the learned morphological patterns of the classifiers. Overall, this work provides an impact-oriented validation of synthetic biomedical imaging data and underscores the necessity of task-level evaluation as a prerequisite for the responsible use of generative models in ART and broader healthcare applications.

items.title: STUDENTS’ PERCEPTIONS ON AI TRANSLATION: A THEMATIC ANALYSIS
items.abstract: In addition to the availability of machine translation technologies such as Google Translate, people now have the option of employing Generative AI to carry out the translation tasks. GenAI is capable of producing translations in any language in a quick and efficient manner. Students in English department who might be interested in pursuing careers as language translators in the future, should have mastered artificial intelligence technologies in order to thrive in the world that is always changing. The purpose of this study is to investigate the students’ perceptions regarding the employment of artificial intelligence tools such as ChatGPT for translating texts. This study was presented with two research questions, which are as follows: To what extent do students position AI translation tools in relation to human translation? When it comes to the employment of artificial intelligence for translation, what benefits and concerns shapes students’ attitude toward AI translation use? In order to collect the necessary information for this study, interviews were conducted with twenty-two students from English department at Binus University who were enrolled in Translation course. The interview transcripts were used as the data for this study, and they were analysed qualitatively using thematic analysis framework developed by Braun and Clarke (2006). There are three fundamental steps involved in doing thematic analysis. Starting with initial open coding, which involves classifying data into codes. The second step is grouping the similar codes and finally, defining and naming the themes for each group. Results show that five themes appear in this analysis. These are: conditional acceptance of AI translation, perceived advantages of AI translation, concerns about overdependence, human superiority in meaning, and ethical and institutional boundaries. The findings suggest that even though artificial intelligence translation is effective, it is still a limited tool that must continue to be controlled by humans.

items.abstract: The development of digital technology, artificial intelligence, environmental concerns, and changing workforce needs has encouraged organizations to adopt more sustainable approaches to talent management. This study aims to examine the development of sustainable talent management, identify its key practices, and analyze the role of digitalization, artificial intelligence, employee skill development, motivation, and retention in supporting organizational sustainability. This study employs a qualitative approach using a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) based on the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Relevant studies were identified through systematic searches of selected databases, screened according to predetermined inclusion and exclusion criteria, and analyzed using content analysis and thematic synthesis. The findings indicate that sustainable talent management has evolved from a short-term, performance-oriented approach toward a more strategic and long-term perspective that emphasizes organizational sustainability and employee development. Its key practices include talent attraction and selection, competency development, employee motivation, and retention, supported by digital technologies and artificial intelligence. However, the implementation of these technologies requires continuous employee skill development and a human-centered approach to ensure that technological advancement remains aligned with employee and organizational needs. The study concludes that sustainable talent management integrates technological, human, social, and environmental aspects to support organizational sustainability and long-term organizational resilience.

items.title: Synthesis of Reliable Logic Question Answering Data for Large Language Model with Aid of Operations Research Program
items.abstract: Logical reasoning is a highly valued capability in language models. However, high-quality logical reasoning data remain scarce, while manual data creation is costly and time-consuming. We introduce Operations Research Aided Synthesis (ORAS), a solver-verified, two-layer incremental framework for synthesizing logic question-answering data. ORAS leverages operations research techniques to systematically generate high-quality datasets for evaluating large language models (LLMs) and, when used for training, improving their reasoning capabilities. ORAS's pipeline integrates mathematical programming methods to generate question-answer pairs, and then employs a dual-phase approach: the first phase uses optimization algorithms to construct and evaluate the logic systems by solving the problem using a mathematical solver. The second phase translates the logic system to human-readable problems and generates answers according to the information from the mathematical solver. The fine-tuned model achieves a 22%-33% (percentage point) improvement in accuracy on in-sample tests and a 4%-22% (percentage point) improvement on similar out-of-sample tests.

items.title: Texture Representations in Deep Neural Models and Humans
items.abstract: Visual perception is often studied through the lens of object recognition. However, a large fraction of visual experience concerns image properties that are not naturally described in terms of discrete objects or categories. Visual textures provide a useful method to investigate this complementary aspect of vision, as they can be described through image statistics while spanning a wide range of perceptual and semantic complexity. In this thesis, I investigate how textures are represented in deep neural networks and humans, combining texture synthesis, representation analysis, computational modeling, and psychophysics. I first explored whether the naturalistic texture representations introduced by Gatys et al. (2015) could be combined with the latent space of a Variational Autoencoder to construct a controllable generative model of naturalistic textures. Although the complete model did not achieve the intended performance, the experiments isolated the texture representation proposed by Gatys as the most robust component of our framework and motivated a direct investigation of its representational properties. I then studied texture representations coded as Gram matrices across a diverse set of convolutional neural networks trained for object recognition. Texture information increased with network depth, but the resulting representations recovered only part of the categorical structure of natural textures defined by human judgment. Crucially, their quality was not correlated with measures of neural or behavioral alignment in object recognition. This dissociation indicates that being a good model of the ventral visual stream in an object recognition setting does not necessarily imply representing textures in a human-like way. Finally, I extended this analysis beyond convolutional architectures by comparing one CNN with three Vision Transformers across textures of progressively increasing complexity and with human performance in a psychophysical discrimination task. Vision Transformers formed substantially more consistent representations across texture types than the CNN, and these representational relationships were significantly better aligned with human perception. Taken together, these results show that texture perception provides a complementary benchmark for computational models of vision and exposes limitations within the dominant object recognition paradigm. More broadly, I suggest that understanding biological visual representations requires models and evaluation criteria that account not only for object identity and semantic content, but also for the statistical and contextual structure through which visual appearance is organized.

items.title: THE EFFECTIVENESS OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN IMPROVING STUDENTS’ CRITICAL READING SKILLS AT EFL STUDENTS OF SULTAN AGENG TIRTAYASA UNIVERSITY
items.abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in improving students’ critical reading skills in higher education. As digital technologies increasingly shape learning environments, AI offers potential to enhance higher-order thinking. This research employed a quantitative approach using a quasi-experimental one-group pretest–posttest design. The participants were 30 sixth-semester students enrolled in the Qualitative Research on ELT course at Universitas Sultan Ageng Tirtayasa, selected through purposive sampling. The instrument was a standardized critical reading test measuring students’ ability to identify main ideas, analyze arguments, evaluate evidence, detect bias, and draw conclusions. It included multiple-choice and short-response items to assess analytical comprehension. The treatment integrated AI-based tools for text analysis, summarization, argument mapping, and reflective questioning. Students also compared their interpretations with AI-generated feedback to enhance metacognitive awareness. The intervention was conducted over four meetings under guided supervision. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and a paired-sample t-test. The findings revealed a statistically significant improvement in students’ posttest scores compared to pretest results at the 0.05 level. These results indicate that AI can effectively support critical reading development and foster deeper engagement with academic texts in EFL contexts.

items.title: The flipped classroom model in medical education: A PRISMA-based systematic review
items.abstract: The flipped classroom (FC) model has obtained collective attention in medical education for its potential to enhance student engagement, active learning, and knowledge retention.This study systematically reviews the report on flipped classrooms in medical education using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta- Analyses (PRISMA) framework. Articles were retrieved from reputable databases, including PubMed, Medline, OVID, ACM, ScienceDirect, Taylor & Francis, MDPI, SAGE, SpringerLink, Wiley, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar.The 34 studies were identified exploring flipped classroom teaching approaches to enhance medical education. Review focuses on the tools and technologies employed such as video creation, learning management systems, podcasts, online assessments, and collaborative platforms as well as pedagogical strategies implemented across medical courses.This study focused on flipped learning in higher education. Future research should examine its application in other educational settings, including schools, vocational, technical, and professional training. Emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and augmented reality warrant investigation for their impact on student engagement and learning outcomes across disciplines. Further studies should also explore the influence of cultural and geographical factors on flipped classroom implementation and effectiveness. Additionally, research is needed to determine how flipped classroom activities can be tailored to specific learning objectives, student needs, and subject areas. Finally, longitudinal studies are recommended to assess the long- term effects of flipped learning on student achievement, retention, and academic success.

items.title: The interplay of mathematics anxiety, academic grit and learning engagement: A random-intercept cross-lagged panel analysis
items.abstract: Mathematics anxiety, academic grit, and learning engagement are central to children's mathematics learning, yet their longitudinal interplay remains insufficiently understood. This study examined dynamic associations among these constructs by following 3354 Chinese third- to fifth-grade students across three waves: December 2024, June 2025, and December 2025. To capture dimension-specific processes, six random-intercept cross-lagged panel models were estimated by crossing two dimensions of mathematics anxiety (learning and evaluation) with three dimensions of learning engagement (behavioral, cognitive, and emotional). Results indicated that within-person increases in mathematics learning and evaluation anxiety were prospectively associated with decreases in subsequent academic grit and learning engagement across dimensions. Within-person increases in behavioral, cognitive, and emotional engagement generally predicted lower subsequent mathematics anxiety and higher academic grit. Academic grit showed reciprocal associations with mathematics anxiety and indirectly linked mathematics anxiety to subsequent behavioral engagement; however, corresponding indirect effects involving cognitive and emotional engagement were less consistent. Educational relevance and implications statement This study followed Chinese upper elementary school children over one year to understand how mathematics anxiety, academic grit, and mathematics learning engagement develop together. The findings showed that when children experienced higher levels of mathematics anxiety, whether during learning or evaluation, they tended to show lower subsequent academic grit and lower behavioral, cognitive, and emotional engagement in mathematics. In turn, greater engagement was followed by greater academic grit and lower mathematics anxiety. Moreover, behavioral, cognitive and emotional learning engagement were indirectly associated with lower subsequent mathematics evaluation anxiety through academic grit. These findings suggest that, in mathematics education, encouraging children to “try harder” or exert greater behavioral effort in mathematics is valuable but may not be sufficient. Teachers should also carefully design instructional materials and learning activities that foster children's emotional and cognitive engagement in mathematics. Such efforts may support the development of academic grit and potentially contribute to reducing mathematics anxiety, particularly in evaluation situations.

items.title: The Invisible Handshake
items.abstract: This chapter aims to examine the role played by artificial intelligence in determining the consumer behaviors and buying patterns of children in a digital environment. The chapter focuses on the mechanisms employed by artificial intelligence in marketing, which include collecting consumer data, tracking consumer behavior, persuasion architecture, artificial influencers, hyper-personalization, the Internet of Toys, and voice assistants. The chapter is also concerned with the psychological and emotional triggers employed by artificial intelligence in marketing to consumers, which include fear of missing out, gamification, and reward-based engagement systems. The chapter is concerned with the ethical issues associated with artificial intelligence marketing to consumers, which include issues related to consumer data privacy, manipulation, transparency, and the lack of regulations. The chapter is also concerned with emerging trends in artificial intelligence marketing to consumers, which include considerations related to marketing ethics

items.title: The Misplaced Variable
items.abstract: Generative AI policies often center on whether tools should be permitted, restricted, or detected, yet these questions do not address how students learn to select and evaluate academic support. This chapter introduces CLEAR—Clarify, Locate, Engage, Assess, and Revise/Reflect—an instructional cycle developed through practitioner action research in online first-year composition. Grounded in self-regulated learning, Universal Design for Learning, resource literacy, and instructor-modeled GenAI use, CLEAR positions GenAI as one optional resource within a broader support system. A comparative study included 11 matched participants across SRL-only, AI-only, and CLEAR conditions. The missing UDL-only group prevented the planned factorial analyses, while small samples and measurement limitations restrict the findings to exploratory patterns. CLEAR is therefore presented as a theoretically grounded, human-centered framework that makes resource judgment visible and teachable.

items.title: The psychological effect of gamification mechanism in XR immersive environment on user willingness to behave
items.abstract: With the rapid landing of XR technology in the fields of architecture, education, medical and other fields, how to effectively guide user behavior through interaction design and content mechanism has become the core topic of human-computer interaction research. This paper examines how gamification mechanisms in an XR immersive environment influence users' behavioral intentions. Drawing on self-determination theory as the overarching framework and incorporating spatial narrative structure and the Octalysis framework, it systematically examines the mediating roles of the three basic psychological needs—autonomy, competence, and relatedness—in the immersive experience. The study uses a combination of literature review and theoretical analysis, and constructs a theoretical model of "gamification elements → psychological needs to meet → willingness to act" through the depth analysis of typical XR cases such as medical training, building space guide, safety education and other types of XR cases. The study suggests that XR's distinctive sense of presence and interactivity may amplify the psychological effects of gamification drivers, such as a sense of mission and progression, while excessive competition and manipulative design may undermine intrinsic motivation.

items.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in Learning Writing of the Indonesian and Philippine Students
items.abstract: The integration of technology, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), has transformed foreign and second language learning, including the teaching and learning of writing. AI-based tools can help students find references quickly, paraphrase sentences, translate texts, and check grammar and sentence structure. This study investigated the kinds of AI tools used by Indonesian English as a Foreign Language (EFL) students and Philippine English as a Second Language (ESL) students in learning writing, how they used these tools across the stages of the writing process, and the weaknesses and ethical issues they perceived. A descriptive qualitative design was employed. The participants were students of the English Education Department of Universitas Islam Negeri (UIN) Sultan Aji Muhammad Idris Samarinda, Indonesia, and seven students enrolled in English-related programs at Central Mindanao University, the Philippines. The data were collected through interviews, observation, and documentation, analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, and validated through triangulation. The findings showed that the Indonesian students used a wide range of tools, namely QuillBot, Grammarly, ChatGPT, DeepL, Perplexity AI, and Essay Writer, whereas the Philippine students relied mainly on ChatGPT, followed by Grammarly and Gemini. In both contexts, AI was used throughout the writing process, most intensively at the drafting stage and, among the Philippine students, also at the editing stage. The students acknowledged that AI sometimes produced inaccurate or overly general information and expressed concerns about dependency, while most Philippine students did not disclose their use of AI to their lecturers. These findings suggest that the students used AI selectively, according to their needs and abilities, and that clear institutional guidance on the responsible use of AI in writing is needed.

items.title: These Robots Speak With No Accent
items.abstract: This chapter examines the socio-linguistic implications of Large Language Models (LLMs) and their use as automated editing tools within higher education. Used as de facto writing tutors, tools like ChatGPT and Gemini often enforce a narrow “one English” framework that privileges dominant norms while marginalizing multilingual and multidialectal voices. Drawing on critical AI, algorithmic justice frameworks and on critical language studies frameworks, this chapter explores how AI guidance can reinforce racial and sexist language biases under the guise of data neutrality. Through an analysis of language guidance in experiments involving racially and identity-prompted revisions, the chapter demonstrates how AI-driven standardization undermines linguistic diversity, authenticity, and free expression. This chapter aims to inform educators and administrators about algorithmic biases and to offer strategies that maintain academic rigor while validating students' authentic written voices.

items.title: Toward Intelligent Power Transformer Diagnostics: From Multi-Source Condition Monitoring to Digital Twins
items.abstract: Power transformers are critical assets in modern power systems, and their reliability directly affects grid security, resilience, and continuity of electricity supply. Their condition progressively evolves under interacting electrical, thermal, mechanical, chemical, and environmental stresses, making reliable condition assessment and early detection of degradation essential for effective asset management. Over the past decades, a wide range of diagnostic techniques has been developed, including dissolved gas analysis (DGA), furan and other physicochemical analyses, dielectric response measurements, frequency response analysis (FRA), and partial discharge (PD) monitoring. While these techniques remain indispensable, no individual method provides a complete representation of transformer condition, and their isolated or periodic application offers limited capability for tracking degradation trajectories and supporting prognosis. This review critically examines the evolution of power transformer diagnostics from conventional condition-assessment techniques to Artificial Intelligence (AI), multi-source data integration, hybrid and physics-informed modelling, and Digital Twin technologies. Particular attention is given to the capabilities and limitations of machine-learning and deep-learning approaches, including data representativeness, generalization, interpretability, uncertainty, and field validation. The emerging role of hybrid physics–data models and Digital Twins in integrating measurements, asset history, physical knowledge, and data-driven inference is also examined. Key challenges related to field-data availability, standardization and interoperability, cybersecurity, explainable and trustworthy AI, and dynamic model updating are discussed. Finally, a perspective toward 2040 is presented, highlighting the expected transition from periodic and isolated diagnostics toward integrated monitoring, uncertainty-aware prognosis, and dynamically updated decision-support frameworks for transformer asset and fleet management.

items.title: Training for Entrepreneurial Skill Development
items.abstract: This chapter examines the critical role of training in developing entrepreneurial skills and competencies necessary for fostering balanced global development. Drawing on recent literature, the chapter explores theoretical foundations of entrepreneurship education, pedagogical approaches, competency development frameworks, and the integration of digital technologies in entrepreneurial training. The analysis reveals that effective entrepreneurial skill development requires a multifaceted approach combining experiential learning, virtual entrepreneurship practice, competency-based frameworks, and strategic integration of artificial intelligence and digital ecosystem support. The chapter synthesizes evidence on entrepreneurial leadership development, innovation capabilities, and the impact of structured training programs on business competencies.

items.title: Transformations in the Didactics of Foreign-language Literature in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education is transforming how literary texts are read, interpreted, linguistically mediated, and assessed, as well as how the significance and cultural status of their authors are conceptualised. This article examines transformations in the didactics of foreign-language literature, with particular emphasis on Italian literature and the teaching of Italian as a foreign language. It explores the potential of generative AI for personalised learning, linguistic support, engagement with authentic literary texts, comparative analysis of human-generated and AI-generated interpretations, translation, the development of intercultural competence, and the cultivation of AI literacy. Particular attention is devoted to the methodological potential of the Italian literary tradition, extending from Dante and Petrarca to contemporary Italian literature with examples such as Pirandello and Calvino. The central hypothesis is that artificial intelligence should be regarded neither as a substitute for the professor or for the practice of literary reading, nor merely as a technical instrument or as a means of employing specialised software. The analysis suggests that a more appropriate framework for philological education is a human-centred pedagogical model for the teaching of literature and foreign languages at university level. Within such a model, technological tools, software applications, and algorithms function as instruments for fostering critical thinking and for integrating traditional and contemporary approaches into academic communication and university teaching. Artificial intelligence can be productively employed in the formulation of questions by both lecturers and students throughout the educational process; it can support interpretation and comparative analysis, facilitate the verification of claims and arguments, and, in certain contexts, encourage critical reflection on the reading process itself. In conclusion, the article proposes an expanded didactic model that integrates literary, linguistic, intercultural, digital, and AI literacy, thereby reconceptualising the teaching and learning of foreign-language literature in the context of contemporary higher education. Keywords: foreign-language literature, Italian literature, literary didactics, artificial intelligence, academic communication, philological education.

items.title: Translating Food Pairing Fundamentals into Flavor Pairing for Within-Product Flavor Creation
items.abstract: Abstract Food pairing has attracted a significant amount of research interest in recent decades, especially regarding food-beverage combinations. The concepts used in food-beverage pairing could be similarly applied to flavor recipe creation, where flavor-pairing helps guide ingredient selection to produce enjoyable flavor profiles. However, presently, there is no research focusing on within-product flavor pairing properties that explain why certain combinations are perceived as pleasant beyond empirical observation or cultural convention. Therefore, this review aims to (1) translate the scientific understanding of food pairing into within-product flavor creation by reviewing the history of food pairing, elucidating the mechanisms and their impact factors governing food pairing effects, and assessing food pairing major principles and hypotheses; and (2) propose a flavor pairing approach framework in within-product flavor creation by examining sensory-based methodologies for evaluating flavor pairing effects, instrumental approaches for characterizing flavor-associated compounds, databases of flavor molecules, and emerging predictive approaches (e.g., machine learning and artificial intelligence) for within-product flavor pairing prediction and design. Overall, this review seeks to provide an integrated understanding of food pairing principles and use this knowledge as a scientific foundation for translating food pairing concepts into within-product flavor pairing, advancing both scientific practical applications in flavor design and innovation.

items.title: Understanding the CSR – AI Paradox: The Duality of Health Innovation and Environmental Responsibility in Consumer Perceptions
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in healthcare presents a paradox at the intersection of corporate social responsibility (CSR) and environmental sustainability. While AI‐driven health innovations promise life‐saving benefits and social good, their development often entails substantial carbon emissions that contradict environmental commitments. This study investigates the CSR–AI paradox by examining how consumers perceive and respond to the duality of health innovation and environmental responsibility in AI‐enabled healthcare products. Drawing on cognitive dissonance theory, moral licensing, and greenwashing frameworks, we conducted a scenario‐based experimental study to analyze consumer reactions to discrepancies between firms' environmental, social, and governance (ESG) claims and actual carbon footprints. We introduce and operationalize the concept of Carbon Accountability Elasticity (CAE) as a conceptual framework to quantify and guide analysis of trade‐offs between health utility and environmental accountability. The results reveal that greenwashing—particularly vague or unsubstantiated ESG claims—triggers significant consumer disappointment, reduces willingness to pay, and erodes trust, especially when high carbon footprints are disclosed post‐purchase. However, consumers demonstrate greater tolerance for environmental costs in the case of life‐critical innovations, such as AI‐powered cancer screening, highlighting a moral licensing effect. These findings underscore the importance of transparent ESG reporting and authentic sustainability practices in AI healthcare innovation. The study offers theoretical and managerial insights for advancing responsible innovation that aligns social benefit with environmental stewardship, supporting both sustainable development goals and stakeholder accountability.

items.abstract: Inspecting the connection among digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI), as well as the synthesis of inclusive environment of learning in the awareness among tourists sector is the article's primary goal. It tackles the issue of how this technological synthesis can augment educational accessibility and participation for a range of scholar demographics. The investigation employs a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative surveys and qualitative interviews to gather data from educators and scholars. Key outcomes demonstrate that digital transformation considerably promotes inclusivity in learning experiences, while AI plays a critical mediating function in personalizing education and catering to expert scholar requirements. In order to incubate more equitable environment of learning s, educational institutions should strategically incorporate digital tools along with artificial intelligence (AI) into their curricula, as per to the outcomes. Future initiatives assimilate comparative investigations across various educational contexts.

items.title: WHAT CAN YOU SEE: A MULTIMODAL ANALYSIS OF KNOWLEDGE CONSTRUCTION IN ENGLISH TEXTBOOK
items.abstract: This study investigates how knowledge is constructed in an English textbook through a multimodal perspective grounded in Kress and van Leeuwen’s (2006) theory of visual communication and informed by systemic functional views of meaning-making (Halliday, 1994). Framed by the inquiry “What Can You See?”, the research explores how visual and verbal elements interact to shape the organization, sequencing, and presentation of knowledge in primary-level English language learning materials. Rather than treating images as supplementary decorations, textbooks are approached as multimodal meaning-making environments in which images, layout, typography, and written language collaboratively structure how learners encounter, categorize, and interpret new concepts (Jewitt, 2009). Adopting a qualitative descriptive approach, the study analyzes selected units from a widely used primary English textbook to identify recurring patterns in visual representation and their relationship to knowledge types. The analysis reveals that knowledge is predominantly constructed through concrete visual categorization and structured textual reinforcement. Illustrations emphasize clear participant boundaries, frontal orientations, simplified backgrounds, and stable visual configurations that support recognition and conceptual grouping. Textual components function to guide labeling, identification, and short definitional statements, reinforcing foundational linguistic concepts through repetition and structured sequencing. Drawing on the Revised Bloom’s Taxonomy (Anderson & Krathwohl, 2001), the findings indicate that the textbook primarily facilitates factual and conceptual knowledge, with cognitive processes centered on remembering and understanding. Tasks and visual prompts are designed to encourage recognition, naming, matching, and basic comprehension, while higher-order processes such as analysis, evaluation, or creation appear minimally within the examined units (Kan et al., 2023). The interaction between visual and verbal modes suggests that images function as central organizing frameworks that anchor linguistic knowledge in observable, classifiable, and concrete forms. In this configuration, knowledge is not merely transmitted but visually structured to shape how learners cognitively engage with language content. By examining knowledge construction through multimodal interaction, this study contributes to broader discussions on how instructional materials structure learning experiences in English language education. The findings highlight the importance of deliberate visual-textual integration in curriculum design and material development, emphasizing that multimodal configurations actively influence the types of knowledge foregrounded and the cognitive engagement promoted in classroom contexts.

items.title: When college students perceive GAI feedback as credible: the role of perceived GAI feedback credibility in promoting deep learning through cognitive engagement
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) has rapidly developed in higher education and has raised new questions from an educational psychology perspective. Why does GAI feedback promote meaningful learning for some college students but fail to produce similar learning benefits for others? To answer this question, this study develops a theoretical framework based on Information Processing Theory, Elaboration Likelihood Model, and Constructivist Learning Theory. This study examines how perceived GAI feedback credibility influences college students’ deep learning and explores the mediating role of cognitive engagement in this relationship. This study adopts a stratified simple sampling method and collects questionnaire data from 506 undergraduate students and uses structural equation modeling (SEM) to examine the proposed model. The results show that perceived GAI feedback credibility has positive relationships with both cognitive engagement and deep learning. In addition, cognitive engagement plays a significant mediating role between perceived GAI feedback credibility and deep learning, suggesting that credible GAI feedback may support deep learning by encouraging college students to engage in cognitive processing and reflective thinking. This study extends research on learning psychology in GAI-supported learning environments by explaining how college students evaluate and process GAI feedback. The findings indicate that the influence of GAI feedback on learning does not simply result from the technology itself. Instead, college students’ judgments of feedback credibility and their following cognitive engagement play important roles in shaping deep learning processes.

items.title: Within-person reciprocal processes between AI feedback literacy and agentic engagement: a three-wave random-intercept cross-lagged panel study
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) feedback has become a pervasive feature of university learning, yet whether students’ capacity to engage productively with such feedback co-develops with their broader learner agency remains poorly understood. Drawing on student feedback literacy theory, self-determination theory as a supplementary motivational lens, and the mutualism principle, this study tested whether AI feedback literacy and agentic engagement reciprocally predict each other over time at the within-person level and exploratorily examined whether they share a stable trait-level association. A three-wave panel study of 480 Chinese undergraduates ( N = 399 with complete data across all waves), with measurements at six-week intervals across one semester, was analyzed using a random-intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM). At the between-person level, students who scored systematically higher in AI feedback literacy across the semester also scored systematically higher in agentic engagement, with a moderate and statistically significant trait-level correlation between the two random intercepts ( r = 0.315, p < 0.001), supporting Hypothesis 1. At the within-person level, both cross-lagged pathways were positive and significant: deviations in AI feedback literacy predicted later deviations in agentic engagement ( β = 0.222, p < 0.001), and the reverse pathway was likewise significant ( β = 0.263, p < 0.001). A Wald test indicated that the two reciprocal pathways did not differ significantly in magnitude (Δ B = 0.002, p = 0.972), consistent with a symmetric mutualism. A model comparison confirmed that the RI-CLPM provided substantially better fit than a traditional cross-lagged panel model, with the RI-CLPM revealing substantially larger within-person reciprocal effects once stable trait-level covariation was properly isolated. The findings extend the mutualism principle from a coupling of person-internal constructs to a coupling between a person-internal competency and a person-environment behavioral interface. They also raise the possibility, in a Confucian Heritage Culture context where agentic engagement has historically been culturally muted, that AI feedback may offer a less culturally-loaded venue in which students can exercise agency. The study repositions AI feedback literacy from a static skill into a dynamic developmental resource that is constituted, in part, by the very engagement it enables.

items.abstract: Introduction: Healthcare systems are increasingly complex and variable in the digital era. Nurses must process large volumes of information and make clinical decisions under time constraints, which increases their cognitive load, while conventional nursing documentation offers limited insight into clinical reasoning and learning from actual practice. Objective: To synthesize knowledge on Focus Charting and explain the role of its Focus–Data–Action–Response (F-DAR) structure in reducing cognitive load, supporting clinical reasoning, promoting proactive patient safety in line with Safety-II, and enabling artificial intelligence (AI) applications in digital health systems. Methods: A narrative review was conducted using a systematic literature search of CINAHL, PubMed, Scopus, ThaiJO, and Google Scholar between March 2025 and March 2026. Thai- and English-language publications from 2000 to 2025 were eligible. Of the 198 records identified, 65 were included and analyzed using content analysis combined with conceptual synthesis. Results and Conclusion: Five key themes emerged: (1) the nursing process provides the professional logic underpinning meaningful documentation; (2) the F-DAR structure functions as a condensed nursing process that systematically links data, decisions, interventions, and outcomes, and has the potential to reduce redundancy and cognitive load while supporting clinical reasoning; (3) compared with narrative and SOAP formats, F-DAR is distinguished by its explicit documentation of patient responses; (4) the Response component captures work-as-done and nurses’ adaptations, thereby facilitating learning consistent with Safety-II; and (5) well-structured F-DAR data provide a foundation for health information systems and AI applications in nursing, provided that data governance and nurse oversight are maintained. Direct empirical evidence of the effect of F-DAR on cognitive loads is limited. Focus Charting has the potential to reduce cognitive load, support clinical reasoning, promote Safety-II learning, and provide a foundation for digital nursing innovations. Experimental studies are required to confirm its effectiveness in the Thai healthcare context.

items.title: “Spirituality as a Predictor of Work–Life Fusion Among Healthcare Professionals: An Empirical Investigation”
items.abstract: This study investigates the influence of spirituality on the management of work-life integration among healthcare professionals, highlighting a comprehensive amalgamation of personal, professional, and emotional aspects.In the demanding healthcare environment, professionals often face stress, emotional fatigue, and ethical dilemmas that impact their health and performance.The study examines the influence of spiritual orientation, as manifested through mindfulness, compassion, purpose, and inner balance, on individuals' ability to reconcile their professional and personal lives.An examination of essential aspects of spirituality, such as spiritual resilience, integration, compassion, and spiritual sensitivity, is conducted to comprehend their impact on work-life integration.The results show that spirituality is an important mental resource that helps people be more emotionally resilient, make better moral choices, and be happier with their lives in general.Moreover, the findings indicate that promoting spirituality within healthcare organizations can enhance employee well-being, fortify organizational culture, and elevate the quality of patient care.This study adds to the growing conversation about how to include spirituality in human resource management and occupational health practices in the healthcare field.

items.title: A comparative study of Talkpal.AI-mediated and task-based instruction in relation to EFL students’ uncertainty-related speaking anxiety and metacognitive awareness in speaking: Insights from self-regulated learning theory
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated speaking applications increasingly extend English as a foreign language (EFL) oral practice beyond limited classroom time, yet evidence remains scarce on whether GPT-powered tools such as Talkpal.AI offer advantages over established instructional approaches. Grounded in self-regulated learning (SRL) theory, this quasi-experimental pretest–posttest study compared Talkpal.AI-mediated instruction, task-based instruction, and traditional instruction among 81 Chinese university EFL students in three intact classes: Talkpal.AI (n = 27), task-based (n = 26), and control (n = 28). Uncertainty-related speaking anxiety and metacognitive awareness in speaking were assessed using validated measures. Data were analyzed using MANCOVA with pretest scores as covariates, followed by univariate ANCOVAs and Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. Results showed a significant overall group effect and significant between-group differences for both outcomes, with large effects. The Talkpal.AI group showed the most favorable adjusted posttest profile, followed by the task-based group; both groups showed more favorable outcomes than the control group. From an SRL perspective, structured AI-mediated speaking cycles involving goal setting, repeated practice, monitoring, and reflection may reduce speaking anxiety while strengthening metacognitive awareness. Pedagogically, guided Talkpal.AI rehearsal can be integrated as out-of-class preparation for classroom speaking tasks, supported by brief reflection activities that reinforce strategic regulation and reduce evaluative pressure.

items.title: A hybrid approach to service performance measurement in the era of artificial intelligence: Integrating BERT-based aspect-based sentiment analysis and synthetic data
items.abstract: This study advances aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) by examining how data quality and human–AI collaboration enhance the reliability of service performance measurement from online reviews. A hybrid-validated dataset and transformer-based models are developed to assess whether ABSA can generate attribute-level performance signals from restaurant reviews. A four-study framework is employed: Study 1 constructs a hybrid-validated dataset by integrating rule-based, large language model-assisted, and human-coded labels; Study 2 benchmarks model variants; Study 3 applies the optimal model to TripAdvisor reviews to derive aspect-level sentiment scores; and Study 4 evaluates their complementarity with structured ratings. Results show that hybrid validation improves model performance. ABSA-derived features provide moderate explanatory power and, when combined with structured ratings, achieve comparable performance to ratings alone. These findings suggest that ABSA complements rather than replaces structured evaluations, offering scalable text-based signals for service performance assessment.

items.title: A hybrid explainable artificial intelligence framework for equitable prediction and analysis of postnatal care uptake in Ghana: Integrating ensemble learning, counterfactuals, and causal inference
items.abstract: Objectives To develop and validate a hybrid, equity-focused artificial intelligence (AI) framework for predicting and analysing postnatal care (PNC) uptake among women in Ghana, with emphasis on minority-class sensitivity, model interpretability, and actionable intervention insights. Study design Cross-sectional, secondary analysis of nationally representative survey data. Methods Using data from the 2022 Ghana Demographic and Health Survey (n = 3314), we developed a hybrid AI framework combining ensemble learning (Logistic Regression and Support Vector Machine with soft voting and threshold tuning), explainable AI (SHAP analysis), counterfactual reasoning (DiCE), and causal inference (doubly robust estimators for average and conditional average treatment effects). The Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique (SMOTE) was applied to address class imbalance and stratified 5-fold cross-validation was used for model evaluation. Doubly robust causal inference was conducted using the econml library, with propensity score modelling used to account for treatment assignment, and positivity and exchangeability assumptions assessed through covariate overlap diagnostics. Results The ensemble model calibrated at a threshold of 0.45 achieved a Class 0 recall of 0.31 and an area under the precision-recall curve (AP) of 0.97, outperforming all individual baseline classifiers. SHAP analysis identified maternal age, education level, wealth status, caesarean section, and sex of household head as the most influential predictors of PNC non-utilization. Counterfactual analysis revealed that minimal, actionable changes including increased media exposure, improved educational attainment, or change of residence could shift individual predictions from non-utilization to utilization of PNC. Causal inference demonstrated significant heterogeneity in treatment responsiveness, with women aged 25–34, those with secondary education or above, urban residents, and those in female-headed households exhibiting the highest conditional average treatment effects. Conclusions This interpretable, fairness-aware AI framework advances the prediction and analysis of PNC uptake in Ghana. By prioritizing sensitivity to underserved women and integrating explainability, counterfactual reasoning, and causal inference, the framework provides empirical evidence for targeted, equitable maternal health interventions and is transferable to other low- and middle-income country settings.
